title: Cisco Systems Moves Aggressively Into Remote Router/Terminal Server Markets with Four-in-One Product Family
redistribution_notes: Cite/link the Cisco archive rather than reproducing the announcement.

claims_extracted.claim: Cisco's 1992 communications-server family explicitly targets both remote-router and terminal-server functions in one product family.
claims_extracted.notes: Supports role convergence; it does not prove Cisco products descend from DEC or X.25 PAD implementations.

claims_extracted.claim: The 500-CS provides 8 or 16 asynchronous ports, RS-232/RS-423 interfaces and hardware/software flow control, replacing Cisco's earlier STS-10x terminal-server model.
claims_extracted.locator: Two Hardware Platforms Maximize Flexibility section
claims_extracted.notes: Create exact 500-CS/STS-10x artifact records on the product-archaeology pass.

claims_extracted.claim: The ASM-CS supports up to 112 ports and combines serial interfaces with Ethernet or Token Ring plus Cisco communications/routing software.

notes: Primary contemporary evidence that terminal-server and remote-router/access roles were converging within commercial product families by 1992.
